correctness.rationale: For each affine point the discriminants of all conic intersections are derived exactly. Distinct nonzero offsets make every nonempty product of quadratic discriminants squarefree in odd characteristic. The Weil bound gives \(d(P)=q/2^{\ell-1}+O_\ell(\sqrt q)\) uniformly in the constants, so the full-secant hypergraph has uniformly growing positive degrees and bounded pair codegree. All stated Pippenger–Spencer covering hypotheses hold for fixed \(\ell\); the common point at infinity takes one extra vertical line. Finite checker directly replayed and agreed but does not substitute for the general argument.

value.rationale: The new uniform sharp leading constant is the missing upper side of a natural finite-geometry covering problem explicitly highlighted by the primary paper as its irreducibility obstruction. It is valid simultaneously for all choices of distinct shifts and arbitrary fixed component count. Its character-sum-to-incidence-cover mechanism is nontrivial; it clarifies that the covering asymptotic is \(q/2\) rather than \(q/(2\ell)\) despite the degree \(2\ell\). No effective small-field formula or complete cover classification is claimed.
